beats.say: Suppliers want to see how their products sell.
beats.label: Suppliers
beats.head: How are my products selling?

beats.say: And a partner wants joint insights, but must never see customer rows.
beats.label: A partner
beats.head: Joint insights, no customer rows

beats.say: The old way is to export files, and send copies. Copies go stale, and they leak.
beats.label: The old way
beats.head: Copies go stale, and leak

check.prompt: What does a subscriber to your listing get?
check.why: A linked dataset reads your live data. Nothing is copied.

beats.say: The new way: share live. Do not copy.
Think of a library. You lend the book. You do not print a new one for every reader.
beats.label: Think of a library
beats.head: Lend the book, do not reprint it

beats.say: Analytics Hub works like that. It is now called BigQuery sharing.
beats.label: The tool
beats.head: Analytics Hub (BigQuery sharing)

beats.say: You publish a listing in an exchange. The subscriber gets a linked dataset, read only.
beats.label: How it works
items: You: a listing in an exchange

beats.say: No data is copied. It is always current. And the subscriber pays for their own queries.
beats.label: Why it is good
beats.head: No copies. Always current.

beats.say: And the partner who must not see rows?
Use a data clean room. Both sides bring data. Only combined, aggregated answers come out.
beats.label: Data clean room
beats.head: Only aggregated answers come out

beats.say: And egress controls on a listing can block copying and exporting.
beats.label: Extra lock
beats.head: Egress controls block exports

beats.say: The trap: scheduled exports to partners, when a live listing avoids copies.
beats.label: Exam trap

beats.say: Share live with Analytics Hub. And use a clean room when rows must stay hidden.
beats.label: Station 4.3

beats.say: Line four, done. Try the checkpoint below.
